timeline.description: University students organized demonstrations over the government's public-sector job quota system. The movement expanded throughout July.

timeline.event: Students attacked during demonstrations in Dhaka
timeline.description: Amnesty International documented attacks on demonstrators at Dhaka University involving people believed to be members of the ruling party's student wing.
Protest coordinator Abu Sayed was shot and killed during demonstrations near Begum Rokeya University, a killing documented by human rights investigators.
Internet access was shut down nationwide amid expanding demonstrations and violence; limited services began returning on 23 July.
Authorities announced a nationwide curfew, effective around midnight, amid escalating unrest and the deployment of additional security forces.
The Supreme Court reduced the quota reserved for descendants of independence fighters to five percent; demonstrations continued amid calls for accountability.

timeline.event: Protests regain momentum in early August
timeline.description: Demonstrations expanded again during 1–3 August after a temporary lull following the quota decision.
Amid mass demonstrations, Sheikh Hasina resigned and left for India. The unrest culminated in a change of government.

timeline.event: Muhammad Yunus sworn in as Chief Adviser
timeline.description: Nobel Peace Prize laureate Muhammad Yunus took the oath as head of the interim government, three days after Hasina's departure.
